title: Fibonacci that finishes
description:
Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 ...

The textbook recursive version is correct and hopeless: it recomputes the same values over and over, and `fib(50)` would take minutes.

```cpp
long long fib(int n) { return n < 2 ? n : fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2); }
```

Write `long long fib(int n)` that is still recursive but **remembers** every answer it has already worked out (this is called memoization). A `static std::vector<long long>` inside the function makes a good memory. The tests ask for `fib(90)` and expect it in well under a second.
hints: Before computing, check whether `n` is already in the memory vector and return it if so. After computing a new value, `push_back` it. Because `fib(n - 1)` is evaluated first, the vector always fills in order.
